answer: Observation with PSA monitoring; no adjuvant or salvage therapy is indicated for organ-confined, node-negative, margin-negative disease with undetectable PSA.
Active surveillance (observation is also acceptable given limited life expectancy of about 6 years).
Workup for recurrence after radiation therapy (PSA above nadir + 2) with PSMA PET/CT or other imaging and biopsy as indicated, to guide salvage local therapy options.
Salvage radiation therapy to the prostate bed (PSMA PET-guided), with ADT not routinely added for low-risk disease.
Observation with monitoring; no salvage therapy is recommended given severe heart failure and limited life expectancy of about 3 years.
Metastasis-directed therapy (e.g., SBRT) to the pelvic bone lesions in the oligorecurrent pathway, with or without ADT.
Workup and treatment of high-volume metastatic castration-sensitive disease: ADT plus an androgen receptor pathway inhibitor, with or without docetaxel.
Discontinue active surveillance and offer definitive treatment for Grade Group 3 (intermediate-risk) disease, such as radical prostatectomy, EBRT with or without ADT, or brachytherapy.
